terms.grammar: orbus, orba, orbum with the ablative of what one is bereft of
evidence: Cic. Q. Fr. 1.3.10: fīliī meī, tē incolumī, orbī nōn erunt, of children left fatherless (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Leg. 3.9: plēbs orba tribūnīs, with the ablative of what is lost (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: orbus is bereft, above all of a parent or a child; what is lost goes into the ablative, and on its own the word means an orphan. Mātre orbus is Traupman’s phrase: we have found no classical instance of it with mātre, but the construction is Cicero’s.

sources: Lewis & Short: orbus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 348.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
